newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First says progress made in talks with National.
newsitem.headline: NZ First says progress made in talks with National.

text.p: New Zealand First Deputy Leader Tau Henare said on Wednesday progress was being made following talks with the National Party about forming a coalition government.
"Progress is being made," he told reporters after the talks.
He declined to say what was on the agenda.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger, leading the National Party team, said the talks were constructive.
Asked why party leader Winston Peters did not attend the talks, Henare said: "He foreshadowed a long time ago he would not be at every meeting and today was one of them."
Peters would not attend NZ First's talks with Labour this afternoon. Henare declined to reveal what Peters was doing.
NZ First holds the balance of power after the inconclusive October 12 election.
